astronomy_facts_and_boundaries: Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center and is roughly 26,000 light-years from Earth; that distance is astronomy, not the precession period.
Sagittarius A* is not established as a portal or conduit to an eleventh dimension.

The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy, not a simple torus. Toroidal structures occur in many physical contexts, but calling the whole Milky Way a torus requires a specific mathematical definition and evidence.
Earth's magnetosphere is approximately dipolar near Earth and strongly distorted by the solar wind; the geographic North Pole is not a literal magnetic/toroidal exit portal.
Large-scale cosmic-web filaments and the thalamus can be compared visually or graph-theoretically, but no evidence shows they are exact scaled copies or physically coupled.
Planets do not occupy different spacetime dimensions. Sun/Earth/Moon/Saturn dimensional assignments are project symbolism.

coordinate_discipline.rule: Never call two directions aligned until both are transformed into a common coordinate frame and epoch and their angular separation is computed.
coordinate_discipline.celestial_vector: n(alpha,delta)=(cos delta cos alpha, cos delta sin alpha, sin delta)
coordinate_discipline.separation: cos psi=sin delta_1 sin delta_2+cos delta_1 cos delta_2 cos(alpha_1-alpha_2)
coordinate_discipline.axis_case: For an undirected physical axis use psi_axis=acos(|a dot n|).
coordinate_discipline.local_pointing: Local azimuth/altitude additionally requires observer position and time; do not infer them from account metadata or present location when reconstructing historical claims.

j2000_sanity_check.derived: Great-circle separation Sirius↔Regulus is approximately 57.83 degrees using these catalog coordinates. Distances from the north celestial pole are approximately 106.72 degrees and 78.03 degrees respectively.
j2000_sanity_check.meaning: Neither is collinear with the north celestial pole in this specific physical-coordinate sense. This says nothing against symbolic Dog/Lion/North correspondences; it simply separates them from astronomical alignment.

sirius_regulus_branch.rule: Until the original Axis definition is recovered, do not infer that the terrestrial rotation axis, galactic axis, Sirius or Regulus are collinear.

best_fit_axis_method.problem: If a predeclared set of celestial targets is claimed to share an undirected axis, estimate the axis rather than drawing one by eye.
best_fit_axis_method.solution: The unit eigenvector associated with the largest eigenvalue of M maximizes sum_i w_i(a dot n_i)^2.
best_fit_axis_method.null_rule: For isotropically random directions, proximity within psi_0<=90 degrees of either pole of a pre-specified undirected axis has probability 1-cos(psi_0); correct for search multiplicity if many targets/axes/tolerances were tried.
best_fit_axis_method.project_value: This turns Axis alignment into residual geometry and an explicit null model rather than retrospective line drawing.

torus_recovery_target.historical_hint: The repository's older recovery list explicitly remembers an unresolved '115,000-mile torus calculation'.
torus_recovery_target.current_result: Exact 115,000-mile formula/input geometry was not recovered from the searched Library transcript/export in this pass.
torus_recovery_target.torus_parameters: A ring torus requires major radius R and minor radius r. Surface area A=4 pi^2 R r and volume V=2 pi^2 R r^2.
torus_recovery_target.underdetermination: One remembered length cannot reconstruct a torus. Even if 115,000 miles were the major circumference C_major=2 pi R, it would determine R but leave r, aspect ratio R/r, area and volume unknown.
torus_recovery_target.do_not_reconstruct_silently: Preserve the number as an unresolved historical target until radius/diameter/circumference and physical object are recovered.

precession_eye_target.physical_neighbor: Earth's axial precession has a timescale of roughly 25.8 kyr; precision historical reconstruction requires epoch-dependent precession/nutation standards rather than using one fixed pole.
precession_eye_target.dimension_rule: A period [time] and distance [length] cannot be equated because their bare numerical values resemble one another in chosen units.
precession_eye_target.archive_rule: Keep roughly 26,000 light-years to the Galactic Center and roughly 26,000-year axial precession as different quantities with different dimensions; do not merge them because the numbers are similar.
precession_eye_target.measurement_rule: If the Eye/Axis idea predicts a historical sky relation, compute target-pole separation at the actual epoch using standard astrometry.

scientific_conclusions: Physical North is not one universal vector: geographic, magnetic, celestial, ecliptic and galactic coordinate systems answer different questions.
The phrase 'points to Sirius' is scientifically incomplete until an Axis vector, frame, epoch and tolerance are defined.
The J2000 sanity check shows why symbolic correspondence and physical collinearity must remain separate: Sirius and Regulus are not near the north celestial pole in equatorial coordinates.
Torus reconstruction illustrates parameter identifiability: one remembered measurement cannot determine a two-radius geometry.
The celestial branch gains credibility by making negative results and non-alignments first-class outcomes rather than forcing every motif into physical correspondence.
